meta.description: Performs 3D shape-based similarity searching using ROCS (OpenEye), USRCAT (ultra-fast), Open3DAlign (RDKit), ESPSim (electrostatic), and ShaEP with explicit handling of Tanimoto-Combo (shape + color), shape vs ECFP4 complementarity, conformer-ensemble searching, alignment optimization, and scaffold hopping. Use when searching for shape-mimicking compounds with different scaffolds, identifying bioisosteric replacements, prospective scaffold hopping, or expanding hit series beyond 2D similarity.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 5 cited DOIs (ROCS Hawkins 10.1021/jm0603365, USRCAT Schreyer/Blundell 10.1186/1758-2946-4-27, ShaEP Vainio/Puranen/Johnson 10.1021/ci800315d, Open3DALIGN Tosco/Balle/Shiri 10.1007/s10822-011-9462-9) are real, correctly attributed papers. No invented benchmark numbers presented as literature results; every numeric value in the illustrative code is explicitly labeled a repository starting default requiring calibration, not a validated finding. Unchanged from the pre-fix audit.

practice_boundaries.detail: Compound virtual-screening tool; no diagnostic or prescriptive statements about individuals. Unchanged from the pre-fix audit.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled fallacy detected. The Skill correctly and repeatedly distinguishes normalized shape Tanimoto (0-1), unnormalized O3A score, and ROCS TanimotoCombo (0-2, a sum not an average). Unchanged from the pre-fix audit.

code_usability.detail: 7 of 7 inputs completed; 6 executed real code against installed RDKit 2026.03.6 / ShaEP 1.4.2 / Open Babel 3.1.0 / espsim 0.0.1 with zero syntax or import errors. The Input-4 defect from the pre-fix audit (shape_search_ensemble silently dropping 2/3 library molecules) is fixed and independently re-verified: a fresh re-run of the original audit's exact Input 4 reproducer now scores 3/3 molecules with explicit WARNING lines for partial-convergence drops (1/20 and 4/20 conformers). A second, never-before-used disconnected-fragment case (diphenhydramine hydrochloride, distinct from the pre-fix audit's [Fe+2].[Cl-].[Cl-]) is correctly rejected with a clear reason while a normal molecule in the same batch scores normally.

functional_suitability.note: Fixed: ESPSim now has its own runnable example (EmbedAlignScore), independently re-run on a fresh molecule pair (ibuprofen vs a chloro-analog, different from the fixer's acetanilide pair) -- shape_sim=0.935 in [0,1], esp_sim (default carbo, unbounded)=0.850, renormalize=True bounds it to 0.905, exactly as newly documented. The conformer-ensemble convergence-gating bug is fixed (see reliability). USRCAT, Open3DAlign, ROCS/TanimotoCombo (commercial, correctly flagged unexecutable here) and ShaEP remain correctly covered.

reliability.note: Fixed: shape_search_ensemble now filters to converged conformer ids, scores survivors, drops a molecule only on zero convergence, and prints a WARNING with SMILES + reason for every drop -- independently re-verified on both the original audit's Input 4 library (3/3 now score, was 1/3) and a fresh case. Disconnected-fragment input is now rejected everywhere it can occur (the library loop and examples/shape_search.py's prepare_mol_3d, the latter verified directly to raise ValueError on a fresh salt SMILES and still embed CCO normally). Held at 11/12, not 12/12: no automated regression test accompanies these fixes in the repo (matches the pre-existing maintainability gap), so a future edit could silently reintroduce the same class of bug.

performance_context.note: Unchanged: SKILL.md remains well-layered against usage-guide.md and examples/shape_search.py; no upfront bloat from the additions.

agent_usability.note: Fixed: the Per-Tool Failure Modes table now has an explicit 'Disconnected-fragment (salt) input' row naming the exact mechanism and fix, and the Conformer-Ensemble Shape Searching section's prose now states the partial-drop/full-drop distinction and the printed-warning contract directly -- both gaps the pre-fix audit flagged this category for are closed.

human_usability.note: Fixed: the ensemble path's prior total silence on drops (a forgiveness/communication gap) is closed by the printed WARNING lines, independently confirmed in two separate re-runs.

security.note: Fixed: the data-integrity gap (disconnected-fragment SMILES silently producing physically meaningless conformers) is closed by the upfront GetMolFrags check, independently re-verified with a fresh salt SMILES the fixer did not use.

maintainability.note: Unchanged: clean 3-way split (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/shape_search.py) preserved; redundancy check confirms usage-guide.md still does not restate the new ESPSim or ShaEP mol2-conversion content. No accompanying automated test harness, as before.

agent_specific.note: Fixed: escape-hatch guidance now covers both failure modes the pre-fix audit found (silent ensemble drop; disconnected-fragment blind spot) in the Failure Modes table and the ensemble section's prose. Held at 19/20: the Common Errors table itself (as distinct from Per-Tool Failure Modes) still has no row for the ensemble partial-convergence case.

recommendations.title: obabel --gen3D can warn 'NaN in calculated coordinates' on some fused-ring scaffolds while still producing usable output
recommendations.problem: Building a mol2 for a naphthalene-containing SMILES via the SKILL.md's own obabel --gen3D command printed an Open Babel warning about NaN coordinates during 3D building, even though the final mol2 had valid non-zero coordinates and ShaEP scored it sensibly (not the silent all-zero-coordinate trap the audit env's TOOLS.md separately documents and works around).
recommendations.root_cause: Open Babel's force-field builder can emit an internal NaN warning mid-build on some conformers before recovering; SKILL.md's obabel step doesn't tell the reader to sanity-check the printed mol2 block when this specific warning appears.
recommendations.fix: Add one line to the ShaEP subsection: if obabel prints a coordinate-related warning during --gen3D, inspect the output mol2's @<TRIPOS>ATOM block for non-zero, non-repeating coordinates before trusting the downstream ShaEP score.
